{{Short description|Genus of flowering plants}} {{speciesbox |image = Petiveria - Ehret.jpg |genus = Petiveria |parent_authority = [[Carl Linnaeus|L.]] |species = alliacea |status = G5 |status_system = TNC |status_ref = {{cite web |title=NatureServe Explorer 2.0 |url=https://explorer.natureserve.org/Taxon/ELEMENT_GLOBAL.2.140010/Petiveria_alliacea |website=explorer.natureserve.org |access-date=6 May 2022}} |authority = L.{{GRIN | accessdate=2010-04-05}} |synonyms = ''Mapa graveolens''
''Petiveria corrientina''
''Petiveria foetida''
''Petiveria graveolens''
''Petiveria hexandria''
''Petiveria paraguayensis'' }} '''''Petiveria''''' is a genus of [[flowering plant]]s in the [[Rivina humilis|pigeonberry]] family, [[Petiveriaceae]]. The sole species it contains, '''''Petiveria alliacea''''',{{cite journal |first=Sherwin |last=Carlquist |title=Wood and Stem Anatomy of ''Petiveria'' and ''Rivina'' (Caryophyllales); Systematic Implications |journal=IAWA Journal |volume=19 |number=4 |pages=383–391 |year=1998 |doi=10.1163/22941932-90000659}} is native to [[Florida]] and the lower [[Rio Grande Valley (Texas)|Rio Grande Valley]] of [[Texas]] in the United States,{{cite web |url=http://www.riodeltawild.com/JanJune2004/Petiveria%20alliacea.pdf |last=Mild |first=C |title=Smelly Weed Is Strong Medicine |work=Rio Delta Wild |date=2004-06-26 |access-date=2010-04-05}} Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, and tropical South America. [[Introduced species|Introduced]] populations occur in Benin and Nigeria.{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7FJqgQ3_tnUC |last=Schmelzer |first=GH|author2=Gurib-Fakim, A |title=Medicinal Plants |year=2008 |publisher=Plant Resources of Tropical Africa |isbn=978-90-5782-204-9 |pages=412–415}} It is a deeply rooted [[Herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[Perennial plant|perennial]] [[shrub]] growing up to {{convert|1|m|ft|abbr=on}} in height and has small greenish piccate [[flower]]s. The roots and leaves have a strong acrid, [[garlic]]-like odor which taints the milk and meat of animals that graze on it.Johnson, L. 1999. ''Anamu: Petiveria Alliacea''. 14 pages (paperback). Woodland Publishing. {{ISBN|1-58054-038-4}} (In Spanish). ==Common names== It is known by a wide number of common names including: ''guinea henweed'', ''guiné'' ({{IPA|pt|giˈnɛ|pron}}) in Brazil, ''anamú'' in Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico and Brazil, ''apacin'' in Guatemala, ''mucura'' in Peru, and ''guine'' in many other parts of Latin America, ''feuilles ave'', ''herbe aux poules'', ''petevere a odeur ail'', and, in Trinidad, as ''mapurite'' (pronounced ''Ma-po-reete'') and ''gully root'',Mendes J. 1986. ''Cote ce Cote la: Trinidad & Tobago Dictionary'', Arima, Trinidad, p. 95. and in Jamaica as ''guinea hen weed'' {{cite news |url=http://www.jamaicaobserver.com/news/New-anti-cancer-discovery-from-Guinea-Hen-Weed_16214248 |title=New anti-cancer discovery from Guinea Hen Weed |work=Jamaica Observer |date=2014-03-09}} and many others. ==Description== ''Petiveria alliacea'' is a herbaceous shrub. Leaves are simple, alternate, pinnate in the first order and netted the second order. It has determinate inflorescences. Although the plant is capable of reproducing throughout the year, reproductive activity peaks during a portion of the year that is dependent on geography. For example, in Mexico this period is from September to October, while in Central America it is from July to January. ==Range and habitat== This plant is native to the United States (southernmost Florida and Texas), the West Indies, Mexico, Central America and South America. In southern Florida it has been reported in disturbed areas, maritime, mesic, prairie and [[Tropical hardwood hammock|tropical hardwood]] [[Hammock (ecology)|hammocks]] and [[Midden#Shells|shell mound]].{{cite web |url=http://regionalconservation.org/ircs/database/plants/PlantPage.asp?TXCODE=Petialli |title=''Petiveria alliacea'' L. Guinea hen weed |work=Floristic Inventory of South Florida Database Online |publisher=The Institute for Regional Conservation |access-date=2017-01-06}} In Mexico, ''P. alliacea'' is widely present in corn, coffee and apple plantations.{{cite web |url=http://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/70236 |title=''Petiveria alliacea'' (guinea hen weed) |work=Invasive Species Compendium |publisher=CABI |access-date=2017-01-06}} ==Uses== ''Petiveria alliacea'' is used as a bat and [[insect repellent]].{{cite journal |first1=R. |last1=Pérez-Leal |first2=M. R. |last2=García-Mateos |first3=M. |last3=Martínez-Vásquez |first4=M. |last4=Soto-Hernández |title=Cytotoxic and antioxidant activity of ''Petiveria alliacea'' L. |journal=Revista Chapingo. Serie Horticultura |year=2006 |volume=12 |number=1 |pages=51–56|doi=10.5154/r.rchsh.2005.010.11 |doi-access=free }} ==Phytochemistry== ''Petiveria alliacea'' has been found to contain a large number of biologically active chemicals including [[benzaldehyde]], [[benzoic acid]], benzyl 2-hydroxyethyl trisulphide, [[coumarin]], isoarborinol, isoarborinol acetate, isoarborinol cinnamate, [[isothiocyanates]], [[polyphenol]]s, senfol, [[tannin]]s, and trithiolaniacine.{{cite web |url=https://www.ansci.cornell.edu/plants/medicinal/anamu.html |title=Petiveria alliacea |work=Medicinal Plants for Livestock |publisher=Cornell University Department of Animal Science |access-date=2010-04-04}} The plant's roots have also been shown to contain cysteine sulfoxide derivatives that are analogous to, but different from, those found in such plants as garlic and [[onion]]. For example, ''P. alliacea'' contains ''S''-phenylmethyl-L-cysteine sulfoxides (petiveriins A and B){{cite journal|last=Kubec|first=R|author2=Musah, RA|title=Cysteine sulfoxide derivatives in ''Petiveria alliacea''|journal=Phytochemistry|year=2001|volume=58|issue=6|pages=981–985|url=http://www.rabimusah.com/pdfs/Cysteine%20Sulfoxide%20Derivatives%20in%20Petiveria%20Alliacea.pdf|doi=10.1016/s0031-9422(01)00304-1|pmid=11684199|bibcode=2001PChem..58..981K|archive-date=2017-08-09|access-date=2011-11-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809090154/http://www.rabimusah.com/pdfs/Cysteine%20Sulfoxide%20Derivatives%20in%20Petiveria%20Alliacea.pdf|url-status=dead}} and ''S''-(2-hydroxyethyl)-L-cysteines (6-hydroxyethiins A and B). These compounds serve as the precursors of several [[thiosulfinate]]s such as ''S''-(2-hydroxyethyl) 2-hydroxyethane)thiosulfinate, ''S''-(2-hydroxylethyl) phenylmethanethiosulfinate, ''S''-benzyl 2-hydroxyethane)thiosulfinate and ''S''-benzyl phenylmethanethiosulfinate (petivericin).{{cite journal|last=Kubec|first=R|author2=Kim, S|author3=Musah, RA|title=S-Substituted cysteine derivatives and thiosulfinate formation in ''Petiveria alliacea''--Part II|journal=Phytochemistry|year=2002|volume=61|issue=6|pages=675–680|url=http://www.rabimusah.com/pdfs/Cysteine%20S-Substituted%20Cysteine%20Derivatives_part%202.pdf|doi=10.1016/S0031-9422(02)00328-X|pmid=12423888|bibcode=2002PChem..61..675K|archive-date=2016-03-03|access-date=2011-11-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303193103/http://www.rabimusah.com/pdfs/Cysteine%20S-Substituted%20Cysteine%20Derivatives_part%202.pdf|url-status=dead}} All four of these thiosulfinates have been found to exhibit antimicrobial activity.{{cite journal|last=Kim|first=S|author2=Kubec, R|author3=Musah, RA|title=Antibacterial and antifungal activity of sulfur-containing compounds from ''Petiveria alliacea''|journal=Journal of Ethnopharmacology|year=2006|volume=104|issue=1–2|pages=188–192|url=http://www.rabimusah.com/pdfs/Antibacterial%20and%20Antifungal%20Activity.pdf|doi=10.1016/j.jep.2005.08.072|pmid=16229980|archive-date=2016-03-03|access-date=2011-11-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303174914/http://www.rabimusah.com/pdfs/Antibacterial%20and%20Antifungal%20Activity.pdf|url-status=dead}} Petiveriin also serves as precursor to phenylmethanethial ''S''-oxide, a [[lachrymatory agent]] structurally similar to [[syn-propanethial-S-oxide]] from onion,{{cite journal |vauthors=Kubec R, Kim S, Musah RA |year=2003|title=The lachrymatory principle of ''Petiveria alliacea''|journal=Phytochemistry|volume= 63|issue= 1|pages=37–40|doi=10.1016/S0031-9422(02)00759-8 |pmid=12657295|bibcode=2003PChem..63...37K }}{{cite journal |vauthors=Kubec R, Cody RB, Dane AJ, Musah RA, Schraml J, Vattekkatte A, Block E |year=2010|title=Applications of DART Mass Spectrometry in ''Allium'' Chemistry. (''Z'')-Butanethial ''S''-Oxide and 1-Butenyl Thiosulfinates and their ''S''-(''E'')-1-Butenylcysteine ''S''-Oxide Precursor from ''Allium siculum''|journal= Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry|volume= 58|issue= 2|pages= 1121–1128 |doi=10.1021/jf903733e |pmid=20047275}} but whose formation requires novel cysteine sulfoxide lyase and lachrymatory factor synthase enzymes differing from those found in onion.{{cite journal |vauthors=Musah RA, He Q, Kubec R |year=2009|title=Discovery and characterization of a novel lachrymatory factor synthase in ''Petiveria alliacea'' and its influence on alliinase-mediated formation of biologically active organosulfur compounds|journal=Plant Physiology|volume= 151|issue= 3|pages=1294–1303|doi=10.1104/pp.109.142539 |pmid=19692535 |pmc=2773066}}{{cite journal |vauthors=Musah RA, He Q, Kubec R, Jadhav A |year=2009|title=Studies of a novel cysteine sulfoxide lyase from ''Petiveria alliacea'': the first heteromeric alliinase.|journal=Plant Physiology|volume= 151|issue= 3|pages=1304–1316|doi=10.1104/pp.109.142430 |pmid=19789290 |pmc=2773092}}{{cite journal |vauthors=He Q, Kubec R, Jadhav AP, Musah RA |year=2011|title=First insights into the mode of action of a "lachrymatory factor synthase"--implications for the mechanism of lachrymator formation in ''Petiveria alliacea'', ''Allium cepa'' and ''Nectaroscordum'' species|journal=Phytochemistry|volume= 72|issue= 16|pages=1939–1946|doi=10.1016/j.phytochem.2011.07.013 |pmid=21840558|bibcode=2011PChem..72.1939H }} Domestic animals that consume ''P. alliacea'' can pass the garlic-like odor characteristic of the plant to their meat, eggs and milk. In addition, nitrates in the plant can cause [[Nitrate#Nitrate toxicosis|toxicosis]] in cattle. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category-inline|Petiveria|''Petiveria''}} {{Wikispecies-inline|Petiveria|''Petiveria''}} {{Taxonbar|from1=Q2913546|from2=Q311518}} [[Category:Petiveriaceae]] [[Category:Monotypic Caryophyllales genera]]
